statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 56 in the elevated band on an unrestarted Saudi East-West pipeline, WTI marked $100.05, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, thirteen hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because no window inside this horizon contains a tradeable session. Stress at 56 describes an unresolved Gulf supply picture and a hawkishly priced policy week; under the fixed mapping Stress does not alter the machine state on its own.
headline: Thirteen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI $100.05, and both developments verified this hour lean toward talks rather than escalation: GCC, Iraqi and Iranian foreign ministers are due to meet in Oman on Monday over the Strait of Hormuz, and Riyadh withheld retaliation for the pipeline attacks at Baghdad's request.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The H.15 release for 11 September still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95%, a curve consistent with a hawkish policy path rather than a growth scare.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and already priced. Friday's core CPI rose 0.3% on the month against a 0.2% consensus, with headline CPI at 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, and market pricing for a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September decision moved to roughly 87 to 90 percent from about 72 percent the day before. That meeting also carries a Summary of Economic Projections and a press conference thirty minutes after the statement, a structurally multi-stage sequence, but it falls four days beyond this horizon.

Two energy-supply stories carried into the weekend, and both moved marginally toward de-escalation in the reporting verified this hour. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, with roughly seven million barrels per day of capacity, remains shut as a precaution after drone attacks in the Riyadh and Madinah regions, with no restart date announced; the updated report adds that Riyadh withheld retaliation at the request of Iraq's prime minister and that Baghdad condemned the attacks and opened an investigation. Separately, foreign ministers from the Gulf Cooperation Council, Iraq and Iran are due to meet in Oman on Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, following an earlier agreement on route coordinates. Against that, Houthi forces now hold Yemen's Red Sea coast and Mayyun Island at the Bab al-Mandeb approach. WTI at $100.05 and Brent at $104.61 fell 2.37% and 2.81% on Friday, a decline reported against the Oman talks rather than restored supply.

The resulting shape is a low Tail against an elevated Stress. The pathological price path that Tail measures requires an open venue, repeated extension after failed retracements and an absence of meaningful pullbacks; none of that can occur across a closed weekend, and Friday's own tape showed retracement working in both directions after a hawkish surprise. Stress at 56 records the unresolved supply picture and a policy week that begins on Tuesday, and under the fixed mapping it does not change the machine state by itself.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 10:00 UTC on 11 September to 09:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in a trend-up read with Tail at 15 and 14 as the European advance extended. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then fell to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final twelve slots sit at Tail 5 and 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 81 to 57 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, thirteen hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps to 7, 8 and 9 at roughly four-hour intervals before capping at 10 for the final nine slots as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 56 to a 60 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage with no restart date, WTI marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach, and a 16 September policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to 81, remaining inside the high band because the evidence set is complete and primary-sourced; the limitation is the freshness of price, not the coverage. The named checkpoints outside this horizon are the Monday foreign ministers' meeting in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz and any announcement of a pipeline restart.
